subject.title: fix(onepassword): key pending authorizations by tool call id only

question: Should authorization correlation become a generic host-authoritative tool-invocation contract, or should core explicitly guarantee composable protected parameter injection for security plugins?
rationale: The plugin cannot independently guarantee that a nonce in adjusted params survives other hooks, while changing before_tool_call parameter composition affects every plugin and its precedence/security semantics.

options.title: Add host-authoritative correlation
options.body: Introduce a generic opaque invocation metadata seam unavailable to model input and use it for the 1Password pending authorization lookup.

options.title: Define protected param composition
options.body: Change and document core hook composition so adjusted params are sequentially composed with explicit precedence and add compatibility tests for multiple hooks.

options.title: Pause the plugin fix
options.body: Keep the PR open without landing until the hook contract can carry authorization state without whole-object parameter replacement.

recommendation.title: Add host-authoritative correlation
recommendation.body: Introduce a generic opaque invocation metadata seam unavailable to model input and use it for the 1Password pending authorization lookup.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant history ties @joshavant to the requireApproval and terminal before_tool_call composition semantics that require a core contract decision.
